text:
leo: hi everyone, day 1 q: what's the safest pattern for using Redwood keys in local dev + CI matrix jobs? I have a repo with parallel jobs and worried about hitting 429s or accidentally leaking a key.
kayla: welcome :wave: quick rules: 1) never commit hosted prod keys. 2) use sandbox keys for casual dev. 3) CI should use per-repo service tokens stored in SecretsManager (rotate them). 4) prefer short-lived ephemeral tokens for high-risk pipelines.
leo: ephemeral tokens? how do those work and how do I get one for CI?
devex-bot: ephemeral tokens are issued via the platform service: https://internal.redwood.devex/ephemeral-tokens. Request pattern: POST to the service with repo id and scope; token TTL defaults to 1h. For manual requests, open https://internal.redwood.devex/requests/keys and choose "Temporary CI token".
riya: for matrix CI specifically, we clamp concurrency per job group. Example: in GitLab, use parallel: 4 and add a job-level check that queries the account limits endpoint before starting heavy tests. If remaining tokens < threshold, skip heavy suite.
ops-bot: account limits endpoint: GET https://api.redwood.ai/v1/account/limits. Also inspect response headers on any request: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (unix epoch). We recommend using Remaining/Reset to gate e2e suites.
leo: any code snippet for gating?
kayla: simple bash check for CI (placed in a step before tests):
```bash
REMAIN=$(curl -s -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | grep -Fi X-RateLimit-Remaining | awk '{print $2}' | tr -d '\\r')
if [ -z "$REMAIN" ] || [ "$REMAIN" -lt 50 ]; then echo "Skipping heavy e2e: low quota ($REMAIN)"; exit 0; fi
```
(We log and skip rather than fail so demos don't block pipelines.)
leo: cool. For demos where we need a burst, can we request a temporary burst quota?
devex-bot: yes, request a temporary hosted dev key or short-term quota bump. Include team, demo time window, expected RPS, and whether streaming is used. Internal SLA: expect 48h turnaround for standard requests, faster if you ping #devex.
riya: additional tip: if your tests use streaming, sandbox has much lower concurrent stream slots. For demo spikes use a short-lived hosted token and mark it in the request. Otherwise, replay captured streams in tests.
leo: thanks, I'll set up SecretsManager + ephemeral token flow and add the quota-gating check. Appreciate the pointers :tada:
